messages:
ravi: Heads-up — seeing a sustained spike of 5xx from the GPU serving cluster in us-west-2. Latency up and retries climbing. Looks like traffic is landing on 2 pods (~90% of connections) while others are nearly idle. Any ideas?

devops-bot: ALERT: High 5xx rate on svc/gpu-infer (us-west-2) — 23:12 UTC — firing to #eng-infra

taylor: I can repro. kube-proxy on nodes gw-02/gw-05 show large conntrack entries. Endpoints count is even across nodes but NAT counters are skewed. Could be affinity/conntrack/MTU weirdness.

morgan: Quick outputs:

kubectl get endpoints svc/gpu-infer -o wide
# shows 10 endpoints distributed across nodes

# iptables nat counters excerpt (on gw-02)
Chain PREROUTING (policy ACCEPT 0 packets)
 pkts bytes target
 120000  9.8M KUBE-SVC-XXXX

# same command on gw-09 shows only ~6k packets

morgan: so the service rules are fine but hit counters heavily skewed.

ravi: tcpdump on the overloaded node shows retransmits and a couple of ICMP "frag needed" messages. Notable: some GPU nodes have MTU=9000 (RDMA/NIC tuned) while most infra nodes are 1500. Suspect PMTU blackholing + retries causing probes/timeouts and endpoint flapping.

# tcpdump snippet (truncated)
14:23:12.123456 IP a.b.c.d.https > x.y.z.pkt: Flags [P.], seq 1:1451, ack 1, win 229, length 1450
14:23:12.123789 IP x.y.z > a.b.c.d: ICMP frag needed, mtu 1500
14:23:12.124012 IP a.b.c.d.https > x.y.z: Flags [R], seq 0, ack 0, win 0

taylor: That matches other cases we've seen. If readiness probes time out because of the extra RTT or retransmits, endpoints get removed and kube-proxy (iptables mode) will concentrate traffic on remaining endpoints -> cascade. What's kube-proxy mode on those nodes?

morgan: kube-proxy is running in iptables on all nodes for now (we haven't fully switched to eBPF). I tried enabling net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1 on a test node and saw retransmits drop. But the skew remained until the flapping pod came back (probeDuration was 1s).

ravi: So two contributors: MTU mismatch causing packet fragmentation/ICMP and readiness probe sensitivity removing endpoints under transient loss. Immediate mitigations:
- Normalize MTU across the cluster (set RDMA nodes to 1500 or standardize to jumbo everywhere)
- Enable MSS clamping on overlay (vxlan/geneve) to avoid fragmentation
- Set tcp_mtu_probing=1 as stopgap
- Increase readiness probe timeout/period for the frontend to tolerate brief retransmits
- Consider switching kube-proxy to eBPF for more even LB behavior longer-term

taylor: Agreed. Also restarting kube-proxy will clear stale conntrack/NAT counters but that risks transient connection disruption — schedule carefully. We can also selectively clear conntrack for the service (conntrack -D -p tcp --dport 443 --orig-port-dst 443) but be cautious.

morgan: I'll open a small runbook and do a canary: 1) set probe timeout to 3s on a single deployment, 2) enable tcp_mtu_probing=1 on a host, 3) apply MSS clamp on overlay interface, 4) if stable, roll MTU normalization. I'll monitor 5xx rate and iptables hit distribution.

ravi: Thanks. If the 5xx rate doesn't drop after those mitigations we'll schedule an after-hours maintenance to normalize MTUs and restart kube-proxy across the affected nodes. Ping me on pager if >5% errors persist. :thumbsup:

morgan: will do — creating INFRA-2318, will report back with graphs and logs in this thread.

taylor: FYI for follow-up: evaluate eBPF mode on a non-prod cluster; it tends to avoid this kind of endpoint skew.

ravi: Good plan. Closing for now, keeping thread open until the canary completes.
